init.telegram.setup: Telegram setup: open @BotFather, send /newbot and keep its token private. Send /setprivacy, choose your bot and Disable; remove and re-add it to existing groups after changing privacy. Alternatively make it a group administrator to see ordinary messages. Add the bot to your group and give it permission to send messages. Only explicitly approved TELEGRAM_ROOMS are learned.
init.telegram.owner: Your canonical Telegram owner key (optional; telegram:user:<numeric user ID>, e.g. telegram:user:42; not a username; Enter = no administrator):
init.telegram.rooms: Approved Telegram rooms (comma-separated negative chat IDs or canonical keys, e.g. -100123,telegram:room:-456; Enter = deny all rooms):
init.telegram.next_steps:
1. In @BotFather, use /setprivacy and Disable; remove and re-add the bot to existing groups, or make it a group administrator.
2. Add the bot to your approved group and allow it to send messages. Check TELEGRAM_ROOMS in .env; blank denies all rooms. Set OWNER_KEY=telegram:user:<your numeric ID> for administration.
3. Start the bot: nibby (binary), cargo run --release (source), or docker compose up -d (Docker). Outbound HTTPS long polling works behind NAT; no public webhook port is needed.
4. Open a private chat with the bot and press Start before requesting private administrative results; send /status in an approved group. It learns future/local messages, not old Telegram group history.

telegram.nickname_warning: My chosen personality name cannot change a per-group Telegram nickname; Telegram does not support that.
telegram.history_warning: I learn future messages and locally saved conversation only; the Bot API does not provide old group history.
telegram.commands.private: Administrative results are sent to your private chat. Open my private chat and press Start there first.
telegram.startup.missing: Configure DISCORD_TOKEN or TELEGRAM_TOKEN, or run nibby init.
init.matrix.plaintext: Matrix is plaintext only: encrypted rooms are unsupported. The bot shares its brain across approved rooms; inform members before inviting it.
init.matrix.user: Dedicated bot's full Matrix user ID (required; e.g. @mybot:matrix.org):
init.matrix.token: Matrix access token (required; copy from the bot account's client/dev tools; keep secret; {secret_hint}):
init.matrix.rooms: Approved plaintext room IDs (optional, comma-separated native !room IDs, including !id:server; not #aliases; Enter = owner invitations only):
init.matrix.owner: Your full Matrix user ID (required for approval/admin; e.g. @owner:matrix.org):
init.matrix.next_steps:
1. Use a dedicated bot account on matrix.org or your own homeserver. Keep .env and the state directory private.
2. Create a plaintext room with encryption disabled. Already encrypted rooms cannot be made plaintext; create a new room instead.
3. From the configured owner account, invite the bot. Only explicitly allowlisted rooms or owner-approved invitations may share its brain.
4. Start a Matrix-enabled build: cargo run --release --features matrix. No inbound port is needed; sync uses outbound HTTP(S).
5. As the owner, send !status (or !durum in Turkish), accept the bot's plaintext admin-room invitation, then run !status there. Commands are owner-only; private mind/settings results are never posted to public rooms. Do not invite others or enable encryption in the admin room.
matrix.encrypted_unsupported: Encrypted rooms are not supported yet. Invite this bot to a plaintext room.
matrix.startup.feature_required: Matrix settings are configured, but this build lacks the matrix Cargo feature. Use a Matrix-enabled build or clear all MATRIX_ settings.

help.text:
commands (all slash):
`/reset [all]` resets the channel ban and any open chat
`/news` posts a news item now · `/problem` asks about a code problem · `/wander` runs an agenda browse
`/prank` / `/hack` image prank / hacked-bot bit
`/agents` runs the profiler and the coach now
`/wake` cuts sleep short · `/sleep [hours]` puts it to sleep for testing
`/status` stage, counters, model, thinking, sleep, travel
`/mind [test]` person/topic/event card + menu/buttons for detail modals; `test` feeds the last 30 lines straight to the diarist (mind-pipeline diagnostic)
`/thinking [mode]` thinking mode (show: reply with the thought in a spoiler · hide: "Thinking..." while it works, reply comes after · silent: thinks in the background, leaves no trace · off: requests go out with reasoning disabled)
`/model [id]` shows/changes the model (favorite only)
`/debug [state]` decision traces land in the channel: willingness score/reason, target, mood, silence/reaction, chat closing
`/settings` button-based settings panel: thinking mode, debug, sleep

panel.label.name: Chosen name
panel.field.secret_help: Leave blank to keep the existing secret. Secret values are never shown again.
panel.field.read_only: Managed by the startup environment; change it outside the panel.
panel.setup.claim: Paste the one-use code from the console setup link. It expires after 15 minutes. Claiming grants a restricted setup session; it does not start the bot.
panel.setup.protect: Choose a unique admin password of at least 12 UTF-8 bytes. Keep it in a password manager. This password protects private bot data; it is not your chat-platform token or provider key.
panel.setup.platform: Where would you like your bot to live? Choose one platform to start. Telegram is the simplest option for a first bot. Each platform connects to the same shared brain; use a separate installation for unrelated groups.
panel.setup.provider: Choose a provider and model, then paste the provider key. Models may cost money. The credential test is separate from saving; never assume a model is free.
panel.setup.fit: Choose the bot’s language, timezone and approved conversations. The panel language is independent. Empty Telegram and Slack lists allow no conversations. Matrix accepts only explicit rooms or invitations approved by its configured owner. Existing connections are preserved.
panel.setup.test_not_saved: Testing does not save credentials or finish setup. Unsaved draft credentials expire after 15 minutes; your administrator ownership remains.
panel.setup.privacy: The bot sends conversation content to your chosen AI provider and retains learned memories. Explain this to members before inviting it.
panel.login.password_help: Use your panel admin password, not a bot token or AI provider key.
panel.account.body: Changing your password revokes existing sessions. You will need to sign in again.
panel.account.password_help: Use a unique password: 12–1024 UTF-8 bytes. Never reuse bot or provider credentials.
panel.account.recovery: Lost the admin password? Stop the bot, then run nibby panel reset-password on the bot's machine and restart it. With Docker, stop the service and run docker compose run --rm bot panel reset-password. Recovery is local only; there is no public reset link.
panel.overview.body: Panel health, platform connectivity and model readiness are different. Check each independently.
panel.overview.refresh_error: Could not refresh status. The last displayed snapshot may be out of date; refresh or sign in again.
panel.overview.no_chats: No active conversation. Moods belong to individual conversations; there is no global mood gauge.
panel.overview.growth_help: Growth is lifetime days plus finished conversations, not model training. A name is chosen at the established stage.
panel.overview.sleep_help: While asleep the bot does not speak, but it still listens and learns.
panel.overview.usage_help: Reported token totals since this process started. Cached tokens are part of input, not extra input. Missing usage or cost is not zero; your provider’s billing dashboard is authoritative.
panel.settings.body: Review values and their sources before saving. Configuration file changes require a process restart; validation and credential tests do not save changes.
panel.settings.restart: Saved — restart the bot process to apply configuration changes. No memories or growth counters are reset. For Compose: docker compose restart bot.
panel.settings.pending: Saved settings differ from active settings. A process restart is required.
panel.settings.valid: Values are valid. Nothing has been saved.
panel.settings.model_override: A stored model selection takes precedence over MODEL in the configuration file. Overview shows the effective model.
panel.logs.body: A bounded recent buffer, not a permanent audit trail. Secrets are redacted, but log messages may still include private conversation-related information. Review before sharing. Viewer filters do not change the bot’s log level.
panel.logs.reconnecting: Connection interrupted. Reconnecting; sign in again if your session has expired.
panel.logs.lag: Missing log lines: {count}. The stream or paused buffer could not keep every line.
panel.logs.empty: No recent log lines match these filters.
panel.logs.no_js: Live streaming requires JavaScript. Recent log details, if available, remain readable above.
panel.help.body:
This bot is software, not a person. It uses your AI provider and may incur charges. Conversation content is sent to that provider and learned memories are retained; tell members before connecting.

Start with Overview to distinguish panel health from platform connection and model readiness. If the bot is offline, check token, privileged intents, server membership, channel permissions and access filters. A token test alone does not prove the gateway is ready. Sleep still listens and learns; stealth hides Discord commands, not this authenticated panel.

Growth depends on both lifetime days and finished conversations. It is not model training. A chosen name normally appears only at the established stage. Moods belong to conversations, not the whole installation.

Memory searches every person, topic and monthly event document. Saves preserve previous revisions; if the record changed, compare your draft with the current text instead of overwriting it. Personality edits the actual temperament prose; a later coach run may change it again. Actions covers all sixteen operations with destination and side-effect review, real jobs and duplicate protection. Usage reports only observed provider fields for this process: missing data and monetary cost stay Not reported, not zero.

Settings show active and saved values and their source. Environment-managed settings are read-only. Secret fields are write-only: blank keeps the existing value. File changes require restarting the process; with Compose use docker compose restart bot. Never reset or discard the memory database to apply settings.

Keep the panel on localhost or use an SSH tunnel/VPN. Public exposure requires a reviewed HTTPS proxy configuration; a password alone is not a security perimeter. Logs are bounded and can contain private information even after secret redaction.

If you lose the panel password, stop the bot, run nibby panel reset-password locally on the bot machine, then restart. With Docker use docker compose run --rm bot panel reset-password while the service is stopped. Do not share setup links, provider keys, bot tokens or configuration files.
panel.help.commands_body: Read: /status, /help, /mind and /settings. Runtime controls: /wake, /sleep, /thinking, /model and /debug. Learning and browsing: /mind test=true, /agents and /wander may write memory or spend provider money. Public posting: /news, /problem, /prank and /hack post in chat where supported. Reset: /reset clears conversation state; all=true affects all conversations, not learned memory. Use /help in Discord for current localized command names and options. The Actions page provides these operations as reviewed controls; inspection links are read-only and mutations report actual job status.

panel.auth_busy: Password verification is busy. Please try again shortly.

panel.config.invalid_choice: Choose one of the listed values.
panel.config.too_many_ids: The list contains too many IDs. Reduce its size.
panel.config.invalid_timezone: Use a finite hour offset from −12 to +14; fractional hours are supported.
panel.config.invalid_id: Use a nonzero decimal platform ID. Keep it as text, not a rounded number.
panel.config.invalid_user_key: Use a canonical platform user key, such as discord:user:42 or telegram:user:42. Numeric IDs alone are not accepted.
panel.config.invalid_telegram_rooms: Use comma-separated canonical Telegram room keys (telegram:room:-100123) or nonzero signed chat IDs (-100123). Blank denies every Telegram room.
panel.config.invalid_address: Use a valid bind IP address.
panel.config.too_many_proxies: Too many trusted proxy addresses. Keep the list small and explicit.
panel.config.invalid_model: Enter a nonempty model ID without whitespace or control characters.
panel.config.invalid_url: Enter a complete HTTP(S) URL without embedded credentials.
panel.config.https_required: This endpoint requires HTTPS; insecure remote HTTP is not supported.
panel.config.invalid_origin: Use an HTTPS origin without a path, query, fragment or embedded credentials.
panel.config.io_error: The configuration file could not be read or written. Check the path and permissions locally.
panel.config.conflict: The configuration file changed after this page was opened. Reload before saving; your changes were not applied.
panel.config.too_large: The configuration exceeds the supported size.
panel.config.invalid_encoding: The configuration file must contain valid UTF-8 text.
panel.config.already_active: The runtime is already active. Save configuration changes and restart the process to apply them.
panel.config.lock_error: Configuration access is unavailable. Check local diagnostics.
panel.config.invalid_dotenv: The configuration file has invalid dotenv syntax. Correct it locally before saving.
panel.config.required: This value is required by the selected configuration.
panel.config.platform_required: Configure a Discord bot token, a Telegram bot token, both Slack app and bot tokens, or a complete Matrix connection; platforms can run alone or together.
panel.config.slack_token_pair: Slack requires both the app-level token and the bot token. Supply the missing credential or clear both.
panel.config.invalid_slack_channel: Use native Slack channel IDs beginning with C or G, not channel names or qualified room keys. Blank approves no channels.
panel.config.invalid_matrix_homeserver: Use an HTTP(S) homeserver URL without credentials, query or fragment.
panel.config.invalid_matrix_user: Use the bot account's full native Matrix user ID, such as @bot:matrix.org.
panel.config.invalid_matrix_rooms: Use comma-separated native Matrix !room IDs, not #aliases or qualified room keys. Blank approves only owner invitations.
panel.config.matrix_required: Matrix requires a homeserver URL and a full native bot user ID. Supply the missing field or clear the Matrix configuration.
panel.config.matrix_auth_required: Matrix requires an access token or password. Supply one credential or clear the Matrix configuration.
panel.config.matrix_feature_required: Matrix configuration requires a build with the matrix Cargo feature. Enable the feature or clear every MATRIX_ setting.
panel.overview.matrix_plaintext_notice: Matrix supports plaintext rooms only; encrypted rooms cannot be read or decrypted. Only explicitly allowlisted rooms or owner-approved invitations share the brain.
platform.startup.missing: There is no configured group-chat platform.
panel.config.unknown_field: This setting is not supported by the panel.
panel.config.read_only: This setting is controlled outside the panel and cannot be changed here.
panel.settings.DISCORD_TOKEN.label: Discord bot token
panel.settings.DISCORD_TOKEN.help: Write-only bot credential. Blank keeps the existing token. Test before saving; token validation does not verify privileged intents or channel permissions.
panel.settings.TELEGRAM_TOKEN.label: Telegram bot token
panel.settings.TELEGRAM_TOKEN.help: Write-only @BotFather credential. Blank keeps the saved token; use Clear to remove it. Telegram can run alone or alongside Discord. Requires restart.
panel.settings.TELEGRAM_ROOMS.label: Approved Telegram rooms
panel.settings.TELEGRAM_ROOMS.help: Explicit comma-separated allowlist: signed chat IDs such as -100123 or canonical keys such as telegram:room:-100123. Blank denies all Telegram rooms, including private chats. Requires restart.
panel.settings.SLACK_APP_TOKEN.label: Slack app-level token
panel.settings.SLACK_APP_TOKEN.help: Write-only xapp- credential with connections:write for Socket Mode. Blank keeps the saved token; use Clear to remove it. Both Slack tokens are required together. Requires restart.
panel.settings.SLACK_BOT_TOKEN.label: Slack bot token
panel.settings.SLACK_BOT_TOKEN.help: Write-only xoxb- credential from OAuth & Permissions after installing the app. Blank keeps the saved token; use Clear to remove it. Both Slack tokens are required together. Requires restart.
panel.settings.SLACK_CHANNELS.label: Approved Slack channels
panel.settings.SLACK_CHANNELS.help: Explicit comma-separated native C…/G… channel IDs, not names. Blank denies all Slack channels. Invite the bot to every approved channel; only trusted channels belong in the shared brain. Requires restart.
panel.settings.SLACK_HISTORY_TIER.label: Slack history rate tier
panel.settings.SLACK_HISTORY_TIER.help: Internal: at least 1 second between history calls and up to 100 messages per page. Restricted commercial non-Marketplace apps: at least 60 seconds and up to 15 messages. Default internal; requires restart.
panel.settings.SLACK_TEST_CHANNEL.label: Slack live-test channel
panel.settings.SLACK_TEST_CHANNEL.help: Optional native C…/G… channel ID for deliberate ignored live tests. Leave blank otherwise. This does not approve a channel for learning. Requires restart.
panel.settings.MATRIX_HOMESERVER.label: Matrix homeserver URL
panel.settings.MATRIX_HOMESERVER.help: HTTP(S) URL without credentials, query or fragment. Matrix can run alone or alongside other platforms in a Matrix-enabled build. Requires restart.
panel.settings.MATRIX_USER.label: Matrix bot user ID
panel.settings.MATRIX_USER.help: Full native user ID of a dedicated bot account, such as @bot:matrix.org; not a qualified owner key. Requires restart.
panel.settings.MATRIX_ACCESS_TOKEN.label: Matrix access token
panel.settings.MATRIX_ACCESS_TOKEN.help: Write-only bot account credential, preferred over password login. Blank keeps the saved token; use Clear to remove it. Requires restart.
panel.settings.MATRIX_PASSWORD.label: Matrix account password
panel.settings.MATRIX_PASSWORD.help: Write-only alternative when no token or saved session is available. Blank keeps the saved password; use Clear to remove it. Requires restart.
panel.settings.MATRIX_ROOMS.label: Approved Matrix rooms
panel.settings.MATRIX_ROOMS.help: Comma-separated native !room IDs, including opaque IDs and !id:server, not #aliases. Blank approves only owner invitations, never all joined rooms. Plaintext only; inform members about the shared brain and local/model processing. Requires restart.
panel.settings.OWNER_KEY.label: Platform command owner key
panel.settings.OWNER_KEY.help: Optional canonical user identity, such as telegram:user:42. Takes precedence over legacy OWNER_ID; blank uses OWNER_ID. Invalid nonblank keys are rejected without fallback. This is not a panel administrator account.
panel.settings.OWNER_ID.label: Discord command owner ID
panel.settings.OWNER_ID.help: Legacy optional nonzero Discord user ID for restricted model commands, used only when OWNER_KEY is blank. This is not panel login or a second admin account.
panel.settings.TZ_OFFSET.label: Timezone offset
panel.settings.TZ_OFFSET.help: UTC hour offset from −12 to +14, including fractions. Affects sleep timing after restart; does not change panel language.
panel.settings.OPENROUTER_KEY.label: OpenRouter API key
panel.settings.OPENROUTER_KEY.help: Write-only provider key. Blank keeps the current key. Required when OpenRouter is selected; models may incur charges.
panel.settings.MISTRAL_KEY.label: Mistral API key
panel.settings.MISTRAL_KEY.help: Write-only provider key. Blank keeps the current key. Required when Mistral is selected; models may incur charges.
panel.settings.PROVIDER.label: AI provider
panel.settings.PROVIDER.help: Select OpenRouter or Mistral explicitly. With automatic selection, an OpenRouter key takes precedence when both keys are configured.
panel.settings.MODEL.label: Configured default model
panel.settings.MODEL.help: Provider model ID. A stored runtime model selection takes precedence; Overview shows the effective model. Availability and pricing are provider-specific.
panel.settings.API_URL.label: Custom AI endpoint
panel.settings.API_URL.help: Optional complete HTTPS chat/completions endpoint without embedded credentials. Custom endpoints receive your provider key; use only a service you trust.
panel.settings.FIRECRAWL_KEY.label: Firecrawl API key
panel.settings.FIRECRAWL_KEY.help: Optional write-only key for web extraction. Blank keeps the existing key. Web services may charge separately from your AI provider.
panel.settings.NEWS_CHANNEL.label: News channel ID
panel.settings.NEWS_CHANNEL.help: Optional nonzero Discord channel ID for news posts. The bot must have access and permission; respect server and channel allowlists.
panel.settings.NEWS_RSS.label: News RSS feed
panel.settings.NEWS_RSS.help: Optional credential-free HTTPS RSS URL. Blank uses the bot-language default feed. Remote fetches can fail independently of chat connectivity.
panel.settings.GUILD_ID.label: Allowed Discord server ID
panel.settings.GUILD_ID.help: Optional nonzero server ID. Restricts the bot to this server; blank means no server filter. Check before narrowing access.
panel.settings.CHANNELS.label: Allowed channel IDs
panel.settings.CHANNELS.help: Optional comma-separated nonzero Discord channel IDs. Limits usable conversations; blank means no channel allowlist. IDs remain text.
panel.settings.DEBUG_CHANNEL.label: Decision trace channel ID
panel.settings.DEBUG_CHANNEL.help: Optional channel for decision traces. Debug output can reveal private conversation context; restrict access to this destination.
panel.settings.IMAGE_ANALYSIS.label: Image analysis
panel.settings.IMAGE_ANALYSIS.help: Enable or disable analysis of shared images. Enabled analysis sends image content to the AI provider and may incur charges. Requires restart.
panel.settings.STEALTH.label: Stealth mode
panel.settings.STEALTH.help: Hide Discord commands and platform UI behavior. Does not disable authenticated panel administration. Requires restart.
panel.settings.BOT_LANG.label: Bot language
panel.settings.BOT_LANG.help: English or Turkish for prompts and bot messages. Independent of this panel’s display language; changes require restart.
panel.settings.LOG_LEVEL.label: Operational log level
panel.settings.LOG_LEVEL.help: Select off, error, warn, info, debug or trace. Debug/trace may reveal private content. Viewer severity filters do not change this setting. Requires restart.
panel.settings.LOG_COLOR.label: Console log colors
panel.settings.LOG_COLOR.help: Enable or disable terminal colors, or keep automatic behavior. Affects console output, not the panel. Requires restart.
panel.settings.PANEL_ENABLED.label: Enable panel
panel.settings.PANEL_ENABLED.help: Panel administration is enabled by default. Disabling it requires restart and removes browser access; keep a local recovery path.
panel.settings.PANEL_BIND.label: Panel bind address
panel.settings.PANEL_BIND.help: Defaults to 127.0.0.1. A non-loopback bind exposes the panel to the network; use a reviewed HTTPS proxy or VPN. Requires restart.
panel.settings.PANEL_PORT.label: Panel port
panel.settings.PANEL_PORT.help: TCP port, default 8787. Changes require restart and matching container port mapping. A bind failure does not silently choose another port.
panel.settings.PANEL_CONFIG_PATH.label: Configuration file path
panel.settings.PANEL_CONFIG_PATH.help: Operator-controlled startup path, default .env. Not editable through browser requests. Mount its directory for atomic saves in containers.
panel.settings.PANEL_PUBLIC_URL.label: External panel origin
panel.settings.PANEL_PUBLIC_URL.help: Optional explicit HTTPS origin for a trusted reverse proxy. Not a tunnel or automatic publication. Proxy and host/origin controls must be configured deliberately.
panel.settings.PANEL_TRUSTED_PROXIES.hel: Explicit proxy IP addresses only. Forwarded headers from any other source are untrusted. Leave blank when using direct localhost access. Requires restart.
panel.setup.keep_secret: Leave blank to reuse the saved credential or the credential already verified in this setup session. Secrets are never shown again. Testing keeps a short-lived draft; only Finish saves to disk.
panel.overview.telegram_privacy_warning: Full Telegram group visibility is not confirmed, or a discovered room receives only mentions. The bot cannot learn the full group conversation in limited rooms. In @BotFather, use /setprivacy and Disable, then remove and re-add the bot to existing groups; alternatively make it a group administrator. The Bot API does not provide old group history.
panel.overview.empty_chats: No active conversation yet. The bot needs an accessible joined server and channel; each conversation has its own mood.
panel.overview.next_threshold: Next stage requires at least {target}; both days and finished conversations must qualify.
panel.usage.title: Reported usage · this process
panel.settings.validated: The supplied settings are valid. Nothing was saved.
panel.settings.unknown_help: These entries are not managed by the panel. Their values and comments are preserved when you save.
panel.settings.tests_help: Check Discord, Telegram, Slack or Matrix credentials before saving or restarting. Blank fields use the saved configuration, with environment values taking precedence. Tests do not save changes, update setup drafts or prove that the bot is live. The provider check below does not run a paid completion or test custom endpoints.
panel.settings.test.discord_help: In the Discord Developer Portal, open your application’s Bot page and copy the bot token, not a user token. This checks the verified application identity only. Message Content and Server Members intents, server membership and channel permissions must still be checked separately.
panel.settings.test.telegram_help: Create a bot with the official BotFather account in Telegram using /newbot, then paste its private token. This checks the bot’s identity, not group membership, approved chat IDs or the live polling connection. For normal group conversations, review /setprivacy in BotFather.
panel.settings.test.slack_help: Install your Slack app in its workspace and copy the Bot User OAuth Token (xoxb-). Under Basic Information → App-Level Tokens, create a token (xapp-) with connections:write and enable Socket Mode. Use both tokens from the same app and workspace. This checks bot identity and the app token’s Socket Mode endpoint; token pairing and live socket readiness are checked at runtime.
panel.settings.test.matrix_help: Use a dedicated bot account. Enter its HTTPS homeserver, full user ID (such as @bot:example.org) and access token. Browser tests use an access token only and leave any saved password unchanged. This build must include Matrix support. Authentication does not prove sync readiness or room membership; only unencrypted rooms are supported.
panel.settings.test.blank_saved: Leave blank to use the saved value for this test; environment-managed values cannot be replaced here. Nothing is saved.
panel.settings.test.platform_passed: Platform credentials verified. Nothing was saved; the bot is not proven live.
panel.settings.test.not_live: This result verifies only the returned platform identity. It does not prove a live gateway, polling, Socket Mode or Matrix sync connection, room membership or conversation permissions. Save changes separately, restart if needed, and check Overview for actual readiness.
panel.settings.test_passed: Credential check passed. Nothing was saved. Gateway permissions and model completions are separate checks.
panel.logs.ended: Your session ended. Sign in again to view live logs.
panel.logs.stopped: The bot process is stopping. Reload after starting it again.
panel.logs.reset: The log sequence restarted. Showing the retained buffer.
panel.logs.unavailable: Live logs are unavailable. Reload or sign in again; recent lines remain readable.
panel.logs.no_recent: No operational events have been logged yet. This recent buffer is cleared when the process restarts.
panel.login.body: Enter the administrator password you saved during setup, not your chat-platform token or provider key. Forgot it? Stop the bot and run nibby panel reset-password on the bot's machine before restarting; with Docker use docker compose run --rm bot panel reset-password. There is no public recovery link.
init.slack.app_token: Slack app-level token (required xapp-; Basic Information -> App-Level Tokens -> connections:write; {secret_hint}):
init.slack.bot_token: Slack bot token (required xoxb-; OAuth & Permissions -> Install to Workspace; {secret_hint}):
init.slack.channels: Approved Slack channel IDs (comma-separated C…/G… IDs, not names; Enter = deny all learning):
init.slack.owner: Owner's qualified Slack identity (optional; slack:user:T_WORKSPACE_ID:U_USER_ID; Enter = no owner, Slack administration including status denied):
startup.no_platform: No platform tokens configured. Run `nibby init` to create .env.
startup.slack_token_pair: Slack requires both SLACK_APP_TOKEN and SLACK_BOT_TOKEN.
slack.nickname.unsupported: Slack cannot change channel nicknames; the personality name stays in bot memory.
init.slack.next_steps:
1. Create an app from docs/slack-app-manifest.yml at https://api.slack.com/apps. Keep Socket Mode enabled; check the bot scopes and event subscriptions.
2. Install the app to your workspace (reinstall after permission changes). Create a separate xapp- app-level token with connections:write; never put that scope in bot scopes.
3. Invite the bot to each approved public or private channel with /invite @bot. Set SLACK_CHANNELS to their native IDs before starting; empty means no learning. Only trusted, approved channels belong in the shared brain.
4. Start: nibby (binary), cargo run --release (source), or docker compose up -d (Docker). As the configured OWNER_KEY owner, send !status or @bot status in an approved channel (not /status); blank OWNER_KEY denies Slack administration. Replies are private ephemeral messages. See docs/setup-guide.md#slack-socket-mode for limits and privacy.
panel.memory.description: Browse and correct the shared brain’s people, topics and monthly event documents. Editing does not disable future learning.
panel.memory.index_help: INDEX.md is a compact retrieval pointer, not the complete memory. It is rebuilt automatically after a save; edit the original records below instead. All connected platforms share this brain.
panel.memory.empty: No matching records on this page. Change the search or use the next page if available.
panel.memory.order: Last updated first, with stable identity order for records updated at the same time. Pages include complete records, not the limited retrieval index.
panel.memory.limits_help: The date is display metadata; the revision is the conflict token. Long records can be summarized by a later agent run. JSON requests are limited to 32 KiB; native forms allow 96 KiB for encoding while decoded content stays limited to 24 KiB. Prior content is retained before replacement.
panel.memory.edit_help: Save corrects this revision and preserves the previous content. A later learning run can evolve the record again.
panel.memory.events_help: This is the complete monthly document: both summary prose and raw dated event lines. Neither is hidden or reduced to a bullet-only preview. Older material can be summarized by a later learning run.
panel.memory.name: Display name
panel.memory.favorite_help: The configured favorite’s score is locked at +10 and the favorite note is protected. Identity cannot be changed here.
panel.memory.score_help: An integer from −10 to +10. This changes remembered opinion, not the person’s identity.
panel.memory.lines_help: One item per line. Previous names and tags cannot contain commas; fields use the existing stored person format.
panel.memory.person_help: A single line of text. The canonical record identity comes from the URL, not the display name.
panel.memory.saved: Memory saved. The previous revision was preserved and the derived index updated. The bot can learn and update this record again in a future run.
panel.memory.conflict: Not saved: this record changed after you opened it. Your draft is preserved below; nothing was overwritten.
panel.memory.compare: Compare your draft and current record
panel.memory.copy_help: Select the draft textarea and copy its text (Ctrl+C / Command+C). This works without JavaScript. Reload the current record, then apply any corrections deliberately; there is no automatic overwrite.
panel.memory.draft: Your submitted draft · select and copy
panel.memory.invalid_identity: Choose a valid people identity, safe topic slug or event month (YYYY-MM). Arbitrary storage keys and paths are not allowed.
panel.memory.storage_failed: Memory could not be read or saved. No successful save is being reported; try again after the storage problem is repaired.
panel.memory.not_found: This memory record was not found.
panel.memory.unsafe_person: Structured editing is disabled because this person record contains unknown fields, raw prose or a noncanonical format. The original text is shown read-only so no unrecognized information is silently lost. A format-preserving migration is required before editing it here.
panel.memory.revision_required: Supply the record’s revision: a hidden revision for forms, or the quoted ETag in If-Match for JSON updates.
panel.personality.description: One shared personality and memory across approved conversations. Growth is not model training; mood is temporary and conversation-specific.
panel.personality.core.source: Source: the personality prompt embedded in this binary for BOT_LANG. It changes only when the prompt is rebuilt or a different bot language is activated after restart; browser language does not change it.
panel.personality.core_preview: The bot has not started: this is a compiled preview for the configured BOT_LANG, not an active runtime personality.
panel.personality.temperament.source: Source: huy.md, maintained by the temperament coach. The coach runs with the six-hour background cycle while awake and can also be requested from Actions; it needs message history.
panel.personality.profile.source: Source: profil.md, inferred from recent messages by the profiler. It is refreshed in the six-hour background cycle while awake or by Refresh profile and temperament. This is shared group context, not a separate profile per room.
panel.personality.self.source: Source: kendim.md (not self.md), updated by the diarist when processing finished conversations or queued observations and when the model supplies a changed self-state.
panel.personality.corrections.source: Source: duzeltmeler.md, written by the critic after selected finished conversations. These are behavioral notes, not training or permanent rules.
panel.personality.growth.source: Source: gelisim.md and live lifetime counters. Stages require both elapsed days and finished chats and advance only forward: warming up at 3 days/8 chats, established at 10/25, old hand at 30/80. The bot chooses its name at established. These counters are not model training.
panel.personality.manual_notice: Saving preserves the previous revision and updates the live bot after commit. This is not a permanent pin: a new coach run can evolve or replace this manual edit. Maximum 24 KiB of text.
panel.personality.saved: Temperament saved. The previous revision was preserved and the live cached state was published.
panel.personality.name: Chosen name
panel.personality.mood.source: Source: each open conversation's live state. Mood is not persisted and there is no single global mood. View active conversations on Overview.
panel.personality.refresh_warning: Open the refresh_agents action to run the profiler and then the coach. These model calls may cost money and can replace the current temperament, including manual edits. Review and confirm on the Actions page.
panel.personality.storage_error: Personality storage is temporarily unavailable. Nothing was saved.
panel.personality.revision_required: Supply the current temperament revision in If-Match before saving.
panel.personality.conflict: The temperament changed after you opened it. Your draft was not saved.
panel.personality.conflict_help: Copy your draft from the first text area before reloading. Compare it with the current stored text below. Reload to obtain the latest revision, then deliberately reapply any changes; there is no automatic overwrite.
panel.usage.description: Provider usage retained by this running bot only. Totals reset when the process restarts; this is not persistent billing history or a spending limit.
panel.usage.process_only: Only this_process with category grouping is available; persistent history and model grouping are not reported.
panel.usage.cache_note: Cached tokens are a subset of input tokens, not additional tokens. Do not add cached tokens to input or total usage.
panel.usage.field_reporting_note: These field counts cover observed accounting hooks, including usage received before a stream failed, not every provider attempt. Known totals may be partial when some observations omit this field.
panel.usage.accounting_note: The counted-calls value is the existing usage-accounting counter. Successful calls count decoded responses and streams drained without a read error, including decoded retry replies. Calls with reported usage count actual usage objects, including those received before a stream failed; this count can exceed successful calls. Per-field counters separately show reported and missing token fields. Explicitly reported zero is shown as zero; absent fields are Not reported. No counter covers every provider attempt, so overall reporting coverage cannot be calculated.
panel.usage.unconfigured: No running bot is available. Usage and call counts are Not reported, not zero.
panel.usage.background_note: Includes conversation and background-agent calls recorded by the existing accounting hooks. Diagnostic learning uses the agent's category when recorded; setup credential/model tests are not recorded in this runtime counter. Unknown categories retain their raw identifier. Category call counts are shown only when recorded.
panel.usage.no_categories: No categories have been recorded in this process.
panel.usage.cost_note: The current provider accounting does not retain monetary cost or currency. Not reported is not free or zero. Check the official provider billing dashboard; this panel does not enforce a spending limit.
panel.usage.billing.openrouter: OpenRouter official credits and billing dashboard
panel.usage.billing.mistral: Mistral official console — usage and billing
panel.memory.runtime_starting: The bot is starting and loading its memories. Wait for startup to finish, then save again; your edit has not been saved.
panel.actions.title: Actions
panel.actions.explanation: These controls use the same administration service as chat commands. Choose a trusted destination where needed. Review public posts, memory changes, privacy implications and possible provider charges before execution.
panel.actions.description.status: Read runtime, sleep, model and conversation status; this does not send a message.
panel.actions.description.help: Read the complete action catalog and its safety explanations.
panel.actions.description.mind: Browse learned memory, or run the diarist on up to 30 recent conversation lines. The test writes memory and can spend provider money.
panel.actions.description.settings: Open validated settings and see which changes require a restart.
panel.actions.description.reset: Clear current conversation runtime state, not learned memory. Reset-all affects every conversation in this shared brain. A busy conversation cannot be reset.
panel.actions.description.news: Generate and post a relevant news item to the chosen destination. There may be no relevant news or no generated post.
panel.actions.description.problem: Generate and publicly post a software gripe to the chosen destination.
panel.actions.description.wander: Browse news and update the shared agenda. This may call your provider.
panel.actions.description.prank: Generate an image comment and post a photo. Usable photos and upload permission are required.
panel.actions.description.hack: A public joke with an image, not an actual hack. Usable photos and upload permission are required.
panel.actions.description.agents: Run the profiler, then the coach. This may replace manual temperament edits and spend provider money.
panel.actions.description.wake: Change global sleep state. Existing wake behavior may reply externally to pending mentions or the last conversation.
panel.actions.description.sleep: Sleep for an integer from 1 to 24 hours; default 8. Sleep is global. The bot can still listen and learn.
panel.actions.description.thinking: Leave mode at Read current value, or explicitly choose Show, Hide, Silent or Off. Changes are persisted globally.
panel.actions.description.model: Leave the ID blank to read the current model, enter an ID to validate and persist it, or explicitly restore the configured default. Unsupported provider catalogs are reported, not assumed valid.
panel.actions.description.debug: Explicitly turn traces on or off. Traces may post to external debug destinations and can reveal private conversational information.
panel.actions.effect.privacy: Private conversation information may leave this installation
panel.actions.bot_unavailable: The bot is not running. Complete or repair configuration first.
panel.actions.photos_unavailable: No usable photo is available. Add supported images to the configured photos directory.
panel.actions.destination_unavailable: No ready, approved, bound destination supports this operation.
panel.actions.destination_forbidden: The destination is not an exact approved conversation or thread on this connection.
panel.actions.destination_required: Choose an approved destination for this operation.
panel.actions.unsupported: The destination does not have the required sending, upload or thread capability.
panel.actions.destination_help: Only ready, approved and bound rooms are listed. Names are secondary to canonical identities. A destination is required only for conversation-scoped operations, not reset-all.
panel.actions.model_help: Blank reads the current model. Changing a model persists a global override. For default restoration, leave this field blank and choose Restore configured default.
panel.actions.confirm_help: Check the exact destination, arguments and side effects. Execution starts only after you confirm. Closing the browser after submission will not cancel the job.
panel.actions.global_destination: Global operation; no selected chat destination. Automatic wake replies use pending mentions or the last active conversation.
panel.actions.automatic_destination_help: Taken from pending mentions or the last conversation, not browser input. Global wake behavior may choose between these destinations if runtime state changes before execution.
panel.actions.confirm_required: Explicit confirmation of the destination, arguments and side effects is required.
panel.actions.interrupted: Interrupted. An already committed change or accepted message cannot be undone; check the bot before submitting again.
panel.actions.replay_conflict: This submission key was already used with different arguments or a different destination.
panel.actions.queue_full: The bounded job queue or retained submission store is full. Wait before submitting a new action.
panel.actions.timeout: Execution timed out. A change or message already accepted may still have taken effect; do not blindly resubmit.
panel.actions.read_action: This is a read-only operation. Open its page or use the authenticated GET endpoint; no job was started.
panel.actions.mutation_requires_post: This operation changes state and requires POST with CSRF, arguments and confirmation.
panel.actions.storage_failed: The operation could not complete its memory write or read.
panel.actions.platform_failed: The platform did not accept the operation. Check connection and destination permissions.
panel.actions.operation_failed: The operation failed. Private provider responses and secret details are not shown here.
panel.actions.busy: A conversation is busy. Wait for the in-flight reply before resetting it.
panel.actions.model_validation_unsupport: The configured provider endpoint does not support authoritative model validation. The model was not changed.
panel.actions.result_too_large: The operation returned more data than the bounded job store can retain. Effects may already have taken place; inspect the corresponding read page before retrying.
panel.actions.job_missing: This job does not exist in your session, has expired, or belonged to a previous process.
panel.actions.job_help: This is the actual shared-service outcome. Queued is not delivery. Refresh manually without JavaScript; optional polling is read-only and does not extend your session. Interrupted work may have partially taken effect.
panel.actions.retention_help: Up to 10 jobs may be outstanding, with 2 running concurrently. Up to 128 jobs are retained for 30 minutes after finishing, with a 10-minute execution timeout and 64 KiB result limit. Duplicate keys are bound to this login session. Jobs are not replayed after restart. Shutdown rejects new work and marks unfinished jobs interrupted; already committed writes or accepted messages cannot be undone.
admin.action.silent: The model chose silence; no public message was delivered.
admin.action.no_input: There was no input to process; no records were changed.
admin.action.woke_delivered: Awake; a public wake-up reply was delivered.
admin.action.woke_without_message: Awake; no public wake-up message was delivered.
admin.action.no_transition: Already awake; no sleep-state transition or public message occurred.
admin.action.sleep_extended: Already asleep; a sleep window of {hours} hours was added. No public message was delivered.
admin.action.model_default: Configured default restored: {model}. The saved override was removed.
admin.error.operation: The requested operation failed. No success was reported; check the server logs.
admin.error.busy: A generation is still running in the affected conversation. Try again after it finishes.
admin.error.model_validation_unsupported: Model catalogue validation is not supported for this custom endpoint; the model was not changed.
admin.error.reason.model_id: the model ID must be nonempty and have no surrounding whitespace
admin.error.reason.model_unknown: the model is not listed in the provider catalogue
panel.memory.facts_events_help: One remembered fact or dated event per line. Existing entries stay visible so you can correct them deliberately.
panel.memory.note_help: A short, single-line note about this person. Editing the note does not change their identity.
panel.setup.probe_credential_invalid: Enter the required bot credentials for this platform. The credential format is invalid.
panel.setup.probe_response_invalid: The platform did not return a valid authenticated bot identity. Check the credentials and try again.
panel.setup.probe_request_failed: The credential check could not be completed safely. Check the connection and try again.
panel.setup.probe_identity_mismatch: The authenticated account or workspace does not match the account being configured.
panel.setup.probe_rejected: The platform rejected the credential check. Check the credentials, permissions, and service availability.
panel.setup.probe_response_too_large: The platform returned a response that exceeded the credential-check limit.
panel.setup.probe_platform_invalid: Choose Discord, Telegram, Slack, or Matrix.
panel.setup.access_confirmed: I reviewed access and privacy with the group
panel.setup.not_ready: A successful credential test is not proof of live readiness. Finish saves configuration and starts the bot. Check Overview for the actual connection, membership and permitted conversations. Conversation content goes to your AI provider and learned memories are retained.
panel.setup.more_platforms_help: Start with one platform. Later, enter another platform’s credentials and approved rooms in Settings, save, then restart the process. Existing connections remain configured. All connected platforms share this bot’s memory and personality.
panel.setup.stale_test: This credential test was superseded by another test or platform selection. Test the currently selected platform again.
panel.setup.telegram.name: Telegram
panel.setup.discord.name: Discord
panel.setup.slack.name: Slack
panel.setup.matrix.name: Matrix
panel.setup.telegram.card: A friendly first choice: create a bot with BotFather and add it to your group. One token, no developer console.
panel.setup.discord.card: For your Discord community. Create a bot, enable two required intents and invite it to a server.
panel.setup.slack.card: For a Slack workspace. Import our manifest, install the app and connect two tokens with Socket Mode.
panel.setup.matrix.card: For a Matrix room. Use a dedicated bot account. Plaintext rooms only; encrypted rooms are not supported.
panel.setup.telegram.credentials:
1. Open the official BotFather account in Telegram.
2. Send /newbot and follow its name and username prompts.
3. Copy the bot token here. Keep it private.
For normal group conversations, use /setprivacy in BotFather and choose Disable for this bot. The verified privacy setting is shown at the final step.
panel.setup.discord.credentials:
1. Open the Discord Developer Portal and create an application.
2. Under Bot, create/reset the bot token and copy it here (not a user token).
3. Enable Message Content and Server Members intents. Leave Presence Intent off.
The test verifies the application identity, not gateway intents or channel permissions.
panel.setup.slack.credentials:
1. Download the exact app manifest below. In Slack’s app dashboard choose Create New App → From a manifest, select your workspace and import the YAML.
2. Install the app to that workspace and copy its Bot User OAuth Token (xoxb-).
3. Under Basic Information → App-Level Tokens, generate a token with connections:write and copy it (xapp-). Socket Mode must be enabled.
Use both tokens from the same app and workspace. The test checks bot identity and the app token’s Socket Mode endpoint; pairing and live socket readiness are checked only at runtime.
panel.setup.matrix.credentials: Use a dedicated Matrix bot account, not your personal account. Enter the homeserver, full user ID and an access token for that account. Browser setup verifies Matrix with an access token. This build must include Matrix support. Only plaintext, unencrypted rooms are supported; the bot must not receive or send content in encrypted rooms. The test checks account authentication, not room membership or sync readiness.
panel.setup.telegram.invite: Open the verified bot link to add it to your Telegram group, or add the bot by its username. The approved chat IDs from the previous step control where it can speak; an empty list allows nothing. If privacy is disabled after this test, test the token again to refresh the reported setting.
panel.setup.discord.invite: Use the verified invite link to add the bot to your Discord server. Enable Message Content and Server Members intents in the Developer Portal; keep Presence Intent off. Grant View Channel, Send Messages and Read Message History only in the channels you approve.
panel.setup.slack.invite: The app is installed through Slack’s app dashboard, not a universal invite link. In each approved Slack channel, use /invite @your-bot. The bot must be a member and its channel ID must be approved. An empty approved-channel list allows no conversations. Check Overview after starting for Socket Mode connection and membership.
panel.setup.matrix.invite: In your Matrix client, invite the verified bot account to an unencrypted room. Only explicitly approved room IDs or invitations from the configured Matrix owner can be accepted. No universal invite link is available. Encrypted rooms are unsupported even when their IDs are approved. Check Overview after starting for actual sync and room readiness.
panel.setup.telegram.privacy_on: Privacy mode is ON: Telegram limits which group messages the bot receives. For normal conversation, disable it with BotFather /setprivacy, then remove and re-add the bot to the group if required. Token verification alone does not prove it can read your group.
panel.setup.telegram.privacy_off: Privacy mode is OFF according to the verified bot identity. The bot can receive ordinary group messages, subject to group membership and access rules. Explain this and AI-provider processing to members before adding it.
panel.setup.telegram.privacy_unknown: Telegram did not report a privacy setting. Do not assume it is disabled. Check BotFather /setprivacy yourself; a successful token test is not evidence that the bot receives ordinary group messages.
panel.setup.telegram.acknowledge: I approved the chat IDs and understand the reported privacy mode, group membership and AI-provider processing. A blank chat list denies all access.
panel.setup.discord.acknowledge: I enabled Message Content and Server Members (not Presence), reviewed channel permissions and told members about provider processing and retained memories.
panel.setup.slack.acknowledge: I installed the app, enabled Socket Mode and approved only the channels where members agreed to provider processing and retained memories. Both tokens belong to the same app and workspace.
panel.setup.matrix.acknowledge: I approved unencrypted rooms or configured the Matrix owner who may approve invitations, and told members about provider processing and retained memories. Encrypted rooms cannot be used.
panel.setup.telegram.owner: For Telegram use telegram:user:123456789, replacing the number with your own Telegram user ID (not your username or a group ID).
panel.setup.discord.owner: For Discord, enable Developer Mode, copy your user ID and use discord:user:123456789. This controls bot-owner commands, not panel sign-in.
panel.setup.slack.owner: For Slack use slack:user:T12345678:U12345678 with your workspace ID and your member ID. Both are IDs, not display names.
panel.setup.matrix.owner: For Matrix, a user such as @alice:example.org becomes matrix:user:%40alice%3Aexample.org. Encode @ as %40 and : as %3A. This owner may approve room invitations.
panel.setup.field.DISCORD_TOKEN.label: Discord bot token
panel.setup.field.DISCORD_TOKEN.help: Copy the token from the application’s Bot page. Never paste a user token.
panel.setup.field.TELEGRAM_TOKEN.label: Telegram bot token
panel.setup.field.TELEGRAM_TOKEN.help: Copy the token returned by BotFather after /newbot.
panel.setup.field.SLACK_APP_TOKEN.label: Slack app-level token (xapp-)
panel.setup.field.SLACK_APP_TOKEN.help: Generate an app-level token with connections:write for the same app as your bot token.
panel.setup.field.SLACK_BOT_TOKEN.label: Slack bot token (xoxb-)
panel.setup.field.SLACK_BOT_TOKEN.help: Copy Bot User OAuth Token after installing the manifest-based app into your workspace.
panel.setup.field.MATRIX_HOMESERVER.help: Example: https://matrix.example.org. Use the server for the dedicated bot account.
panel.setup.field.MATRIX_USER.label: Matrix bot user ID
panel.setup.field.MATRIX_USER.help: Full dedicated account ID, for example @mybot:example.org.
panel.setup.field.MATRIX_ACCESS_TOKEN.he: Copy an access token for the dedicated bot account from its Matrix client or account tools. Browser credential verification requires this token. Never use your personal Matrix account.
panel.setup.field.BOT_LANG.label: Bot language
panel.setup.field.BOT_LANG.help: The bot’s prompts and chat messages use this language. Your panel language is independent.
panel.setup.field.TZ_OFFSET.label: Timezone offset from UTC
panel.setup.field.TZ_OFFSET.help: Hours from −12 to +14; fractions work, for example 5.5. This affects the bot’s sleep schedule.
panel.setup.field.OWNER_KEY.label: Bot owner identity (optional)
panel.setup.field.OWNER_KEY.help: A platform-qualified user key grants owner-only bot commands. It is not the panel password. Leave blank if you do not need an owner; keep an existing owner when preserving another connection.
panel.setup.field.GUILD_ID.label: Discord server ID (optional)
panel.setup.field.GUILD_ID.help: Copy the server ID with Discord Developer Mode. Leave blank to preserve the existing unrestricted server behavior.
panel.setup.field.CHANNELS.label: Approved Discord channel IDs (optional)
panel.setup.field.CHANNELS.help: Comma-separated channel IDs. A blank list keeps the existing Discord access behavior; it is not default-deny. Review channel permissions carefully.
panel.setup.field.NEWS_CHANNEL.label: Discord news channel (optional)
panel.setup.field.NEWS_CHANNEL.help: Channel ID for news announcements, subject to permissions and access rules.
panel.setup.field.NEWS_RSS.label: News RSS feed (optional)
panel.setup.field.NEWS_RSS.help: Use a credential-free HTTP(S) feed URL. Leave blank for the language-specific default.
panel.setup.field.TELEGRAM_ROOMS.label: Approved Telegram chat IDs
panel.setup.field.TELEGRAM_ROOMS.help: Comma-separated chat IDs, for example -1001234567890, or telegram:room:-1001234567890 keys. Before starting the bot, privately inspect the official Telegram Bot API getUpdates result after adding the bot and sending a message: chat.id is the group ID; from.id is your user ID. Keep the token private, do not use third-party ID bots, and do not run a second poller alongside this bot. Blank denies all conversations; Overview cannot discover unapproved chats.
panel.setup.field.SLACK_CHANNELS.label: Approved Slack channel IDs
panel.setup.field.SLACK_CHANNELS.help: Open channel details in Slack and copy the channel ID (for example C12345678). Separate IDs with commas. Invite the bot to each approved channel. Blank denies all conversations.
panel.setup.field.MATRIX_ROOMS.label: Explicitly approved Matrix room IDs
panel.setup.field.MATRIX_ROOMS.help: Comma-separated full room IDs, for example !room:example.org, available in room settings. Only unencrypted rooms work. Empty means no explicit approval; only invitations from the configured Matrix owner can add approved rooms.
